He played college basketball for [[North Idaho College]] and [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State University]]. He played in the NBA in 2017–18. ==High school career== Webb played for [[Curtis Baptist High School]] in his hometown of [[Augusta, Georgia]] for two years. He then transferred to The Oaks Virtual School ([[Hilton Head, South Carolina]]), where he averaged 23 points, nine rebounds, and five assists per game while being named team MVP. He also lettered in tennis, soccer, baseball, track, and cross country during his high school career.{{cite web|url=http://www.broncosports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/james_webb_iii_862117.html|title=Boise State bio|work=BroncosSports.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016|archive-date=July 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160729121835/http://www.broncosports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/james_webb_iii_862117.html|url-status=dead}} ==College career== Webb began his college career at [[North Idaho College]]. There, in 2012–13 he appeared in all 31 games, including 17 starts. He averaged 9.2 points and 5.2 rebounds per game, shooting 53 percent from the floor and 76.8 percent from the free throw line, and helped the team reach a 26–5 record. In his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State University]].{{cite web|url=https://nic.edu/news/single.aspx?id=8671|title=NIC's James Webb signs with Boise State University|work=NIC.edu|date=November 14, 2012|access-date=October 29, 2016|archive-date=July 5, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705193543/https://nic.edu/news/single.aspx?id=8671|url-status=dead}} In 2014–15 he was Mountain West Newcomer of the Year, All-MW Second Team, and All-MW Defensive Team.{{Cite web|url=https://broncosports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/james-webb+iii/4266|title=James Webb III – Men's Basketball|website=Boise State University Athletics}} The next year he averaged 15.8 points, 9.13 rebounds (7th in team history), and 1.4 steals per game with a .552 field goal percentage as a junior, leading the Broncos in the first two categories.{{Cite web|url=https://broncosports.com/documents/2023/5/17/Boise_State_Men_s_Basketball_Record_Book_20230517.pdf|title=Boise State Men's Basketball Record Book 20230517|website=Boise State University FORWARD JAMES WEBB III|work=CSNPhilly.com|date=June 24, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2016}} He was named [[Mountain West Conference]] Player of the Week three times, [[USBWA]] All-District VIII, [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] All-District 17 First Team, and earned First-Team All-MW honors.{{cite Webb.jpg|200px|thumb|right|Webb with Delaware in November 2017]] After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Webb joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Ray|last=Boyd|url=http://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2016/07/01/ben-simmons-headlines-sixers-summer-league-roster/|title=Ben Simmons Headlines Sixers Summer League Roster|work=CBSLocal.com|date=July 1, 2016|access-date=January 4, 2017}} On July 8, 2016, he signed with the 76ers,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-announce-samsung-nba-summer-league-roster-signings|title=Sixers Announce Samsung NBA Summer League Roster, Signings|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 9, 2016}} but was waived on October 24 after appearing in six preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-waive-five-players|title=Sixers Waive Five 76ers.{{cite web|url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/3320/|title=SEVENS INVITE 13 PLAYERS TO TRAINING CAMP|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 29, Webb was waived after suffering a season-ending ankle injury.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |title=NBA D-League Transactions |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, |access-date=June 16, 2020}} ===Larisa (2020–2021)=== On September 8, 2020, Webb signed overseas with [[Larisa B.C.|Larisa]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].{{cite web |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola |title=James Webb III signs with Larisa |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/james-webb-iii-signs-with-larisa/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 15, 2020 |date=September 15, 2020}} In 13 games, he averaged 13.3 points and 9.6 rebounds per contest,{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1525728/maccabi-officially-signs-james-webb-iii/|title=Maccabi officially signs James Webb III|date=July 5, 2023|website=Eurohoops}} attracting the interest of bigger clubs. ===Murcia (2021–2022)=== On January 31, 2021, [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]] announced that Webb had joined their team until the end of the season.{{cite web|title=El UCAM Murcia ficha a James Webb III|language=ES|url=http://www.ucamdeportes.com/ucamcb/noticias/el-ucam-murcia-ficha-james-webb-iii|date=January 31, 2021|website=ucamdeportes.com|access-date=January 31, 2021}} He re-signed with the club in the summer of 2021. During the 2021–22 campaign, in 33 league games, Webb averaged 12.1 points and 5.4 rebounds per contest. ===Valencia (2022–2023)=== On July 8, 2022, Webb signed a two-year contract with [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |title=James Webb III, segon fitxatge de la plantilla masculina per a la temporada 22/23 |url=https://www.valenciabasket.com/?p=noticias¬icia=8835 |access-date=July 8, 2022 |website=www.valenciabasket.com |language=es}} In 32 EuroLeague games, he averaged 8 points and 4.1 rebounds in 21 minutes per contest, on 60.9% 2-point shooting and 38.4% 3-point shooting.{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-191644-james-webb-joins-maccabi-on-two-year-deal.html|title=James Webb joins Maccabi on two-year deal|website=basketnews.com}} Additionally, in 26 [[Liga ACB]] matches, he averaged 9.6 points and 4.4 rebounds per contest. ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2023–2024)=== On July 5, 2023, [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=KSKBasket |number=1811339934998855802 |title=Son olarak Maccabi Tel Aviv takımında forma giyen James Webb III Pınar Karşıyaka'mızda!}} === Liaoning
